companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The financial services firm, best known for its prominent investment banking wing and asset management unit, rose two spots on this year’s list, growing revenue 5.7% despite a tumultuous year for the financial sector.

  • The company brought in $68.7 billion in revenue as it opened new offices and expanded its client base.

  • Goldman Sachs’ profits plunged in 2022 as the private and public markets took a beating. The bank brought in $11.3 billion, down 48% from the year prior.

  • In May 2023 the firm reportedly noted in an internal memo its plan to open an office in Abu Dhabi, thus expanding its Middle East footprint.

  • Also in May, the firm agreed to pay $215 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging Goldman Sachs had been underpaying women across several divisions.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Goldman Sachs scored high in gender equality and board expertise. The board of the investment banking giant is led by Adebayo O. Ogunlesi, who is the chairman and managing partner of private equity firm Global Infrastructure Partners and before that was an executive at Credit Suisse. Former president of Harvard University Drew G. Faust is on Goldman’s board, as is Michele Burns, the former CFO of Marsh & McLennan Cos. and CEO at Mercer, the human resources consultancy; Ellen J. Kullman, former CEO of DuPont; and Jan E. Tighe, a former vice admiral of the Navy, where she was deputy chief of naval operations for information warfare and director of naval intelligence.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Coming off a record year in pretty much everything, Goldman Sachs barreled into 2022 ready to do more. The bank reported record net revenues in 2021, while leading the field in announced and completed mergers and acquisitions. It advised on over 200 deals in 2021, which together were valued at more than $1 trillion and represented a dominant market share of more than 24%. Goldman’s impressive 2021 was dampened somewhat by a less-than-stellar beginning to 2022, when it recorded a 42% slump in Q1 profits. The invasion of Ukraine has made the dealmaking environment much less appealing, despite promising growth for Goldman’s wealth management and trading arms.

image.caption: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. headquarters in New York, U.S., on Friday, March 5, 2021.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: In spite of the pandemic, 2020 was a banner year for Goldman Sachs. The bank emerged from the global health crisis with profits up 12% and its highest net revenues in over a decade, boosted by big numbers in trading and dealmaking. Robust results from underwriting and issuance, amid a flurry of IPOs and SPACs (special purpose acquisition companies), helped too. In early 2021, Goldman narrowly evaded hefty losses from its dealings with family office Archegos, whose bets imploded in a fiasco that cost many of Goldman’s peers billions of dollars. Meanwhile, the bank continued its multiyear push into consumer banking, launching Marcus Invest—a belated entry into the popular robo-adviser market catering to Main Street investors.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: For much of its long history, Goldman Sachs served corporations and wealthy clients, not average individuals. In search of more predictable sources of revenue, the bank is now looking to Main Street and beyond. Under the leadership of CEO David Solomon, Goldman Sachs has expanded its push into consumer banking, grown its wealth management business, and launched a treasury services business for corporations, all with the aim of offsetting volatile revenues from trading. Its consumer push is making a big splash: Last year, the bank announced that it was issuing tech giant Apple’s digital-first credit card.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
